title: 9-round AES-256: related-key basic filter for selected subkey recovery

target.description: AES-256 reduced to 9 rounds on 128-bit blocks; initial AddRoundKey k^(0), then rounds 1 through 9, with no MixColumns in the final round. The basic construction guesses 27 bytes in Figure 1 and four bytes of k'^(8), totaling 31 guessed subkey bytes. These guesses determine the late-round integral test.

setting.key_relation: For an unknown base master key L, L_a XOR L has byte a at zero-based master-key byte indices 21 and 25 and zero elsewhere, for every a in 0,...,255. The a=0 key is the base key; total distinct keys is 256.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: Eight varying plaintext bytes cover 2^64 choices under each of 256 related master keys, totaling 2^72 key/plaintext queries.
assumptions: Wrong-subkey rejection uses the paper's heuristic model for zero XOR sums; no numerical whole-procedure success rate is supplied.

The paper presents these constructions as attacks on Rijndael. This record prices the explicitly analyzed selected-subkey filter; complete master-key reconstruction and any repeated filter applications are left for a separate completion-budget review.
Related master keys use a fixed XOR relation, while their expanded-key differences depend on guessed base-key bytes through S-boxes. These are not arbitrary independently selectable subkey oracles.

time.note: Section 4.2 estimates 2^248 guesses and a workload comparable to one encryption per guess. This basic endpoint has different data and key guessing from the partial-sum improvement.

data.note: Total across 256 distinct related keys: 2^64 chosen plaintexts per key. The factor 256 is already included.

memory.note: Neither the basic nor improved related-key construction provides an explicit complete peak-storage budget.

preprocessing.note: Table preparation and setup are described within the construction but not separately priced for this endpoint.

success.description: No numerical success for this exact partial_key_recovery output is given. Section4.2 says enough sets identify the correct guesses; Section4.3 says about32 structures, without a joint error probability. The source 256-key relation and required plaintext compensation are conditions of the balanced identity. The basic 2^72-data endpoint does not inherit the optimized structure count or an invented per-set rejection rate.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit; preserve resource parameters, existing conflicts and full-audit gates. Local source models and conditional relations do not certify whole-output success.
